findings.F1: The idea was rejected by the size of its bar, not by its direction: the criterion asked for a mean strength above 1 (a rise larger than a full usual 1-day move), but after 24-hour drops of 3 to 4 multiples of the 30-day average absolute daily return the next day's strength is 0.32 (+150 bps unusual, t 3.55, 232 cases), and after drops beyond 4 multiples it is 0.48 (+247 bps, t 3.05, 144 cases); both are far above the usual 0.05 of real ideas but far below 1.
findings.F2: The next-day rebound grows with the size of the drop. On non-overlapping 24-hour cases the unusual move is -21 bps (t -3.08, 4991 cases) after drops below 1 multiple, then +37 bps for 1 to 2 multiples (t 3.32), +25 for 2 to 2.5 (t 0.84), +72 for 2.5 to 3 (t 1.87), +150 for 3 to 4 (t 3.55) and +247 beyond 4 (t 3.05); the Spearman rank correlation of drop size against the unusual move is 0.054 beyond 1 multiple.
findings.F3: The test's own cases diluted the effect: its 8426 cases, mostly mild drops, average +11 bps unusual (0.6 times the 19 bps cost), while the 376 cases of drops beyond 3 multiples average +187 bps unusual and +201 bps total over 24 hours (t 4.62), about 10 times the cost of a trade.
findings.F4: After drops beyond 2.5 multiples the 24-hour rebound is positive on all 6 coins: ZEC +277 bps (t 2.85), XMR +212 (t 2.68), XRP +155 (t 2.16), ETH +116 (t 1.81), BTC +100 (t 2.02), and LTC weakest at +43 (t 0.61), with 83 to 103 cases per coin.
findings.F5: The rebound depends on the period: after drops beyond 2.5 multiples it is large in 2018 (+344 bps, t 3.63), 2020 (+208, t 2.22), 2021 (+539, t 3.73) and 2025 (+189, t 2.37), and absent in 2019 (+17), 2022 (-48), 2023 (+1) and 2024 (+9).
findings.F6: The rebound shows at every horizon from 6 hours to 2 days and is clearest over 1 day. After drops of 3 to 4 multiples it is +74 bps over 12 hours (t 2.82), +150 over 24 hours (t 3.55) and +289 over 48 hours (t 3.47). Beyond 3 multiples it is +51 bps over 6 hours (t 4.05). Over 7 days the drop buckets are noisy and not graded (drops of 1.5 to 2 multiples give -207 bps, drops of 2 to 3 multiples give +286).
findings.F7: The shape of the drop matters, but not in a graded way: drops beyond 2 multiples whose last 6 hours carry a third to two thirds of the fall rebound most (+194 bps over 24 hours, t 4.27, 292 cases); drops made mostly earlier rebound less (+60, t 2.27); drops made mostly in the last 6 hours barely rebound (+29, t 0.60).
findings.F8: The book's trades pay after costs, but it does not beat holding. Trades entered on the weakest forecasts net +1.10 % over about 97 hours, and those entered fully long net +0.45 % over about 34 hours. The book's Sharpe of 0.53 is 0.02 below holding's, and its Calmar is 0.25.

ideas.idea: When a coin's 24-hour return, read at an hourly close, is a drop of several times its 30-day average absolute daily return, the price rises over the next 1 day by more than the coin's normal 1-day drift. The larger the drop in those multiples, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader should treat a deep fresh hourly plunge as a reason to buy for a day, because past about 3 multiples the rebound is several times the cost of a trade even though it is smaller than a full usual daily move.
ideas.name: deep plunge next-day rebound

ideas.idea: When a coin's 24-hour return, read at an hourly close, is a drop of several times its 30-day average absolute daily return, the price rises over the next 12 hours by more than the coin's normal 12-hour drift. The larger the drop in those multiples, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader buying a deep hourly plunge can expect most of the rebound within half a day, which is a reason to refuse shorting it over that time.
ideas.name: deep plunge half-day rebound
